title: Broughshane, Racavan & Clough
standfirst: John Glasgow of Cross near Broughshane is a record-supported later Antrim anchor. His connection to the other Antrim and Bann Valley clusters remains unknown.
question: Can the later Broughshane family be placed beside, rather than inside, another Antrim cluster?
answer: The available material supports John Glasgow as a later local household anchor, but no reviewed parish, lease, probate or collateral record connects his family to Kilwaughter, Glenleslie or Bann Valley. It remains a separate study.

chapters.title: A later Antrim household
body: The profile reports John Glasgow of Cross, near Broughshane, and gives a newspaper-style death notice dated 28 July 1836, in his seventieth year.
That notice supports an adult local occurrence and approximate age; it does not name parents, children, holdings or a wider Glasgow connection.

chapters.title: Placed beside other Antrim evidence
body: Broughshane, Racavan and Clough form a sensible local research area for this later household.
Locality and surname alone cannot put John within the Kilwaughter, Glenleslie or Bann Valley families.
